[[File:FreedomCon 2001 SWCCG champions.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Star Wars CCG medalists at FreedomCon 2001.]]
[[File:Virginia Beach oceanfront circa 2001.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Virginia Beach oceanfront hotels, circa 2001. Photo: Fredlyfish4.]]
'''2001 Decipher World Championship''' was the sixth Star Wars CCG World Championship. Play was 15–18 November 2001 at the Sheraton Oceanfront Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia.<ref name="fc-home">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ FreedomCon home page], decktech.net (after the event). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011201221615/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ Internet Archive, 1 December 2001]</ref> [[DeckTech]] billed it as the World Championship at [[FreedomCon]], after [[Decipher]] cancelled DecipherCon 2001.<ref name="tf">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/DecipherCon_2001_72163.asp DecipherCon 2001], TheForce.Net (15 June 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009001958/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/DecipherCon_2001_72163.asp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="holland">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Special_message_from_Decipher_CEO_Warren_Holland_70685.asp Special message from Decipher CEO Warren Holland], TheForce.Net (3 October 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010073714/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Special_message_from_Decipher_CEO_Warren_Holland_70685.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

[[Bastian Winkelhaus]] of Germany defeated [[Martin Akesson]] of Sweden.<ref name="fc-home" /><ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org (World Champions list: "2001 - Bastian Winkelhaus def. Martin Akesson, held at FreedomCon - Virginia Beach, VA"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222454/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Internet Archive, 17 August 2023]</ref><ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040917022419/http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive, 17 September 2004]</ref> [[Monica Jones]], Decipher's vice-president of marketing, wrote on 9 November 2001 that Decipher would not recognize FreedomCon as the World Championships.<ref name="fc-stmt">[http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Deciphers_Statement_About_Freedom_Con_70203.asp Decipher's Statement About Freedom Con], TheForce.Net (9 November 2001; statement by [[Monica Jones]], Decipher V.P. Marketing). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012022154/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Deciphers_Statement_About_Freedom_Con_70203.asp Internet Archive]</ref> The [[Players Committee]] counts the win as the 2001 title.<ref name="awards" /> As FreedomCon champion, Winkelhaus received a Day 2 bye for 2002, as did [[Matt Sokol]].<ref name="hs">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/The_Hyperspace_Lane_to_the_World_Championships_68998.asp The Hyperspace Lane to the World Championships], TheForce.Net (9 February 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009001957/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/The_Hyperspace_Lane_to_the_World_Championships_68998.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

== Cancellation ==

Decipher had scheduled DecipherCon 2001 for the same dates and hotel, with a $50,000 cash purse across its games.<ref name="tf" /> On 3 October 2001 [[Warren Holland]] cancelled the convention, citing September 11 airline-safety concerns. Decipher donated the $50,000 championship purse to September 11 relief.<ref name="cancel">[https://www.theonering.net/torwp/2001/10/03/27367-deicphercon-cancelled/ DecipherCon Cancelled], TheOneRing.net (3 October 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20110413071644/http://www.theonering.net/torwp/2001/10/03/27367-deicphercon-cancelled/ Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="holland" /> On ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' two days later, Holland said the decision was purely about the safety of players, staff and volunteers. Many would travel from around the world, and military alerts in the Norfolk area were high. He said the license and finances played no part.<ref name="rfd99a">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wS84wdG4EUI&t=106s Broadcast 99 - Radio Free Decipher (05 October, 2001): Warren Holland on DecipherCon and 9/11], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 01:46. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-wS84wdG4EUI Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20250101225730/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wS84wdG4EUI watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 1 January 2025). Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 99 transcript]].</ref> The roughly 300 players already qualified across Decipher's games would choose the charities to receive the prize money. Decipher had held back web ticket sales for some time before deciding.<ref name="rfd99b">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wS84wdG4EUI&t=1035s Broadcast 99 - Radio Free Decipher (05 October, 2001): Warren Holland on DecipherCon and 9/11], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 17:15. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-wS84wdG4EUI Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20250101225730/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wS84wdG4EUI watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 1 January 2025). Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 99 transcript]].</ref>

Decipher's Star Wars, Young Jedi, and Jedi Knights licenses ended 31 December 2001. Tournament support moved to the volunteer [[Players Committee]].<ref name="ann">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021203014917/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/index.html Decipher Star Wars index], decipher.com (Wayback 3 December 2002)</ref>

* '''Dates:''' 15&ndash;18 November 2001

== Results ==

The final eight played these Dark and Light decks.<ref name="hayes-tr">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2002-03-11-at-long-last-hayes-freedomcon-trd3493/ At long last, Hayes' FreedomCon TR], Hayes Hunter, DeckTech (11 March 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016161000/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2002-03-11-at-long-last-hayes-freedomcon-trd3493/ Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dt19798">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/19798 All Your Base Are Belong to EUROPE], DeckTech (Bastian "Death Star" Winkelhaus, 21 November 2001). Preservation copies: [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/19798/ Stephen Skilton]; [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/19798/ GitHub Pages]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016161142/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/19798/ Internet Archive]</ref> QMC is [[Quiet Mining Colony / Independent Operation|Quiet Mining Colony]]. LSC is Lightsaber Combat. Players called the Dark [[Tatooine Occupation]] deck All Your Base. Winkelhaus posted that list as ''All Your Base Are Belong to EUROPE''. It starts no Objective and uses two copies of the Effect [[Tatooine Occupation]].<ref name="dt19798" /><ref name="hayes-tr" />

== Play ==

In the quarterfinals Akesson beat [[Brad Reinhold]], Winkelhaus beat [[Kevin Shannon]], [[Brian Hunter]] beat [[Andy McClure]], and [[Hayes Hunter]] beat [[Scott Lingrell]].<ref name="f75427-1300395">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1300395#p1300395 Post by rhendon], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html#p1300395 Internet Archive]</ref> Winkelhaus then beat Brian Hunter. Akesson beat Hayes Hunter.<ref name="f75427-1300395" /> Winkelhaus won both final games. His Quiet Mining Colony beat Akesson's Tatooine Occupation deck. His Tatooine Occupation deck beat Akesson's Lightsaber Combat.<ref name="f75427-1300395" />
